commits.pr_title: [CI][Bench] Keep captured request headers case-insensitive in Responses test
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix the `Benchmarks CLI` failure on main, on both H200 and MI355. It has failed deterministically since #62835 bumped aiohttp to 3.14.5, multidict to 7.1.0 and yarl to 1.25.1:

```
FAILED benchmarks/test_responses_request_func.py::test_request_payload_is_accepted_by_the_server_schema
    assert seen["headers"]["x-request-id"] == "bench-7"
KeyError: 'x-request-id'
```

**Root cause:** the test's aiohttp handler copies `request.headers`, a case-insensitive `CIMultiDictProxy`, into a plain `dict`, then looks keys up case-sensitively. With the new versions, the client sends the well-known header as `X-Request-ID`. A minimal aiohttp server and client, with no vLLM involved, shows the change:

| aiohttp / multidict | Header keys the server sees |
|---|---|
| 3.14.3 / 6.7.1 | `Content-Type`, `x-request-id`, `x-team` |
| 3.14.5 / 7.1.0 | `Content-Type`, `X-Request-ID`, `x-team` |

HTTP header names are case-insensitive, so the benchmark code itself is correct.

**Fix:** keep the headers case-insensitive with `request.headers.copy()`, which returns a `CIMultiDict`. The existing assertions are unchanged.

**Not a duplicate:** no open PR touches this test.

## Test Plan

- Ran the same capture-and-lookup with `.copy()` under both version sets: all three lookups (`x-request-id`, `Content-Type`, `x-team`) succeed on 3.14.3/6.7.1 and on 3.14.5/7.1.0.
- `Benchmarks CLI` CI will confirm the full test.

## Notes

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Quantization][Spec Decode] Load ModelOpt mixed-precision DFlash and DSpark drafts
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix loading of nested ModelOpt `MIXED_PRECISION` checkpoints, quantization
settings for DFlash/DSpark drafts, and per-tensor FP8 normalization on FNUZ GPUs.
This incorporates the parser fix from the
earlier closed, unmerged [PR #36312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/36312)
and adds draft-layer name mapping, regression tests, CI coverage and documentation.

## Claims

- Nested `MIXED_PRECISION` metadata selects the existing `modelopt_mixed` backend.
- ModelOpt draft settings match the weight aliases, runtime module prefix and
  decoder layer offset before quantized layers are constructed.
- Per-tensor FP8 weights and static input scales are normalized for FNUZ GPUs
  such as AMD MI300, using the existing conversion helper.
- Other quantization backends retain their existing quantization-config handling.
  No FP8 kernel changes are needed.

## Validation

The current source passes 24 focused CPU checks and changed-file pre-commit,
including mypy and CI selection. CPU checks used Torch 2.13.0+cpu and
Transformers 5.17.0; current main pins Torch 2.14.0.

AMD CI exposed an existing per-tensor FP8 loader omission: both checkpoint
regressions failed during engine initialization at `input.dtype == weight.dtype`
in [MI300 quantization CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96958#01a16a9a-8a0e-4f38-8027-3356b1307ef8).
The loader retained FN weights while the activation quantizer selected FNUZ.
The fix applies the existing FN-to-FNUZ normalization before requantization,
including both weight and static input scales. The existing regressions now
require the exact platform dtype and input scale. Fresh AMD validation is
pending CI. A CPU check confirmed the conversion preserves dequantized weights, including
negative zero, while doubling both scales.

GPU validation below used vLLM 0.32.0 with the source fixes backported. The
checkpoint-loading regressions are retained, with shared fixture setup and
the existing speculative-metric reader. GPU tests were not rerun for this
cleanup; the full current-main environment and full suites remain untested.

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native/legacy mixed config, uppercase/lowercase | Four mixed-config failures; NVFP4 control passes | All five cases pass |
| Draft mapping, aliases, offsets and Quark preservation | Missing runtime-name mapping | 17 CPU cases pass against real quantization configurations |
| Small mixed Llama checkpoint through `LLM` | Config conversion fails | Loads actual FP8/BF16 layers; nested/flat metadata produce identical completions |
| Small mixed DSpark checkpoint through `LLM` | Missing `fc.weight_scale` parameter | Mixed FP8 `fc`, Markov and offset decoder projections; positive proposals and exact OFF/ON token equality |

Observed errors before the respective fixes:

```text
Value error, Unknown ModelOpt quant algo: MIXED_PRECISION

ValueError: There is no module or parameter named 'fc.weight_scale' in Qwen3DSparkModel. The available parameters belonging to fc (ReplicatedLinear) are: {'fc.weight'}
```

The small GPU regressions create random checkpoints and integer token prompts
locally. Exact comparisons use batch invariance. CI dependencies and the
rendered ModelOpt documentation are updated. Changed-file pre-commit checks
pass, including mypy and CI test selection.

Additional GPT-OSS-20B mixed-FP8 DSpark smoke on B200, TP=1, fixed K=2:

- All 1,120 output tokens across 35 prompts match SpecDec OFF.
- 2,140 tokens were proposed and 16 accepted with normal verification.
- Runtime inspection confirms per-channel weight and per-token activation FP8
  for `fc`, and per-tensor FP8 for the Markov output projection.
- Export files are unchanged.

The GPT-OSS draft was trained for eight optimizer updates and quantized with
synthetic calibration inputs. These are functional smoke results, not a held-out
quality evaluation or a speedup measurement. Other hardware, tensor-parallel
sizes and quantization formats were not tested.

<details>
<summary>Regression commands</summary>

Repository test entrypoints:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py -k modelopt -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_modelopt_mixed_nvfp4.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'draft_quant_config or draft_weight_aliases' -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'nested_mixed_checkpoint or mixed_dspark_checkpoint' -v
```

Earlier GPU execution used the vLLM 0.32 compatibility setup described above.
The regression bodies at that point ran with the real stock test fixture:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -p no:cacheprovider \
  -v -s test_gpu_regression.py
```

Each GPU regression passes after its fix and fails before it with the error
shown above. Current-main GPU execution remains pending.

</details>

## Details

There are two failures. Config conversion rejects nested `MIXED_PRECISION`
metadata before the existing backend can load it. After that is fixed, the
draft loader looks up per-layer settings using runtime names such as `model.fc`,
while the checkpoint names the layer `fc`. It builds an unquantized projection
and then fails to load `fc.weight_scale`.

The shared `map_draft_quant_config` helper in `models/utils.py` maps ModelOpt's
draft settings through the existing weight aliases, module prefix and decoder
layer offset before constructing the layers. Apply this
only to ModelOpt: other backends can use semantic configuration keys or suffix
rules that must not receive a module prefix.

Related work has different scope: [#49900](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49900)
handles `draft_model.` prefixes in another proposer path;
[#53122](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53122) configures draft
quantization aliases and context-KV projection, without this runtime-root and
teacher-layer remapping. No equivalent open PR was found.

AI-assisted implementation and testing using Codex.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][ROCm][Kernel] Add W4A8 int8-dot MXFP4 GEMV for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 d…
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in MXFP4 linear kernel for RDNA3/RDNA3.5 (gfx11) decode. For 1-8 tokens, activations are quantized to int8 per 32-element group, and each group is reduced with `v_dot4_i32_iu8` (`__builtin_amdgcn_sudot4`). E2M1 values times 2 are integers in [-12, 12], so weights map to int8 exactly through a 16-entry table; one fp32 multiply per group applies the E8M0 weight scale, the activation scale, and the 1/2. The approach follows ggml's MMVQ / q8_1 path (llama.cpp, MIT).

- Weights are read in the Quark OCP MX checkpoint layout (`[N, K/2]` uint8 E2M1, `[N, K/32]` uint8 E8M0). No repack, no extra weight memory.
- M > 8 (prefill) runs the same math as `EmulationMxfp4LinearKernel` (activation QDQ, dequant, `F.linear`).
- The M <= 8 / M > 8 split is inside a custom op, so torch.compile and CUDA graphs see one op.

Enable with:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8=1
```

Opt-in because int8 activation rounding differs from the MXFP4 activation QDQ the checkpoint declares. With the flag off, or on non-gfx11 GPUs, kernel selection is unchanged.

Related: #46676 adds a W4A16 (fp32 FMA) scalar + WMMA MXFP4 kernel for gfx1100. This PR is independent: a different algorithm for the small-M regime (2-5x fewer instructions per weight at M = 1-8). The two PRs only touch the same registration lists.

## Benchmarks

AMD Strix Halo (gfx1151, RDNA 3.5), `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`, single stream (`--max-num-seqs 1`), CUDA graphs and torch.compile on, `vllm bench serve` random 128 in / 256 out.

### Comparison with #46676 and emulation (MTP=3, MXFP4 lm_head)

Same model, same machine, all three with the lm_head quantized to MXFP4 (see note). GSM8K 5-shot, lm-eval `local-completions`, greedy.

| Config | Decode kernel (M <= 8) | Decode tok/s | GSM8K (questions) |
|---|---|--:|--:|
| **This PR + MXFP4 lm_head** | W4A8 int8-dot GEMV | **28.89** | **96.51% (1319)** |
| #46676 + MXFP4 lm_head | W4A16 scalar FMA (WMMA for M > 8) | 26.19 | 96.51% (1319) |
| Emulation + MXFP4 lm_head | dequant + `F.linear` | 4.94 | 96.75% (1319) |

- 10% faster than #46676 at equal accuracy, 5.8x faster than the default emulation path.
- For reference, llama.cpp (ROCmFP4 4-bit GGUF, own quantization incl. lm_head) runs 29.1 tok/s at MTP=3 on the same machine.

**Note on activations:** this PR skips the checkpoint's MXFP4 activation QDQ when the flag is on. Decode quantizes activations to int8 per 32-element group (finer than MXFP4); prompts (M > 8) use bf16 activations. Applying the MXFP4 activation QDQ on prompts while decoding with int8 activations dropped GSM8K to ~80% in our runs, so the prompt path is weight-only, matching #46676.

**Note on the MXFP4 lm_head:** the checkpoint ships the lm_head ([248320, 5120]) in bf16, and this PR keeps it that way. For the comparison above, it was quantized to MXFP4 at load time (round-to-nearest, one E8M0 scale per 32 weights), the same for all three configs. It cuts the lm_head from 2.54 GB to 0.68 GB; with MTP=3 the lm_head is read 4 times per step (3 draft + 1 verify), so this is worth ~6 tok/s (22.45 â†’ 28.89). It is not part of this PR and will be proposed separately.

The model card reports 95.0% (bf16 base: 93.3%) with sampling and thinking-mode settings

## Validation

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna.py
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_kernel_selection.py
```

All pass on gfx1151. The new tests cover:

- output vs a reference implementation for M = 1..8, four shapes, fp16 and bf16;
- closeness to the bf16 dequantized result;
- M = 0 and M = 9 rejected by the op;
- `torch.library.opcheck`;
- CUDA graph capture and replay;
- dispatch for M = 1, 8, 9, 64 (kernel vs fallback);
- selection: chosen only with the flag on gfx11; MXFP6 and non-ROCm rejected.

Serve command used:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8=1 vllm serve amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4 \
  --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-seqs 1 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.5 --limit-mm-per-prompt '{"image": 0, "video": 0}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 3}'   # MTP rows only
```

## Details

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `csrc/rocm/mxfp4_w4a8_gemv.cu` | int8 activation quant + W4A8 GEMV, templated on M = 1..8 and fp16/bf16 |
| `csrc/rocm/ops.h`, `csrc/rocm/torch_bindings.cpp`, `CMakeLists.txt` | build and register `_rocm_C::mxfp4_w4a8_gemv` |
| `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/mxfp4/rdna_w4a8.py` | `RdnaW4A8MxFp4LinearKernel`, M-based dispatch in a custom op |
| `vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py` | first in the ROCm MXFP4 kernel list (selected only when supported) |
| `vllm/envs.py` | `VLLM_ROCM_MXFP4_W4A8` (default `False`) |
| `vllm/_custom_ops.py` | Python wrapper and fake impl |
| `tests/kernels/quantization/test_mxfp4_w4a8_rdna.py` | new tests |

- Device code is compiled only for `__GFX11__` (empty stubs elsewhere); the host entry point also checks for gfx11 at runtime.
- One wave per output column; lanes stride over the 32-weight groups along K, then a shuffle reduction. Accumulation is fp32 over the full K, one rounding to the output dtype.

Trade-offs and follow-ups:

- One extra activation-quant launch per linear (fusing it into the GEMV is a follow-up).
- M > 8 dequantizes per call, as the emulation kernel does; a faster prefill path is a separate PR.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][MLA][DCP] Drop VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY

## Purpose

Remove `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY` and always select the DCP multi-token (spec-decode) verify kernel heuristically.

Default behavior is unchanged: the builder now always does what `auto` (the default) did.

- **gfx950:** AITER round-robin asm decode (cprr) when the DCP-gathered head count pads to a native kernel (16/32/64/128), otherwise segmented MLA.
- **gfx942:** segmented MLA where it fits in LDS, otherwise Triton split-KV decode. The env var never affected gfx942.

What goes away:
- `segmented`: the opt-out from cprr on gfx950.
- `asm`: the hard error for head counts cprr can't serve. These now fall back to segmented, as `auto` already did. A config with neither kernel still fails at builder init.

This also clears the way for a follow-up gfx942 verify-kernel work to choose a new assembly verify kernel.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][PERF] Enable MiniMax-M3 Indexer CP
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Adds **indexer-only context parallelism** for the MiniMax-M3 lightning indexer on ROCm (gfx950), opt-in behind `--attention-config '{"indexer_cp": true}'`. Under tensor parallelism each rank owns one index head and scores *every*
128-token block, so at long context every rank re-reads the whole index cache on every decode step and that cost grows linearly with the context. This PR inverts the split: every rank projects **all** index heads and scores **1/P of the
blocks**, then one small exchange gives each rank every shard's candidates for the heads it owns. That turns the index-cache reads into `1/P`, which is the only term here that scales with context.

This PR depends on Aiter PR: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6359

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf][DSv4] Standalone mono decode layer for DeepSeek-V4-Pro on MI355X
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4-Pro mono decode layer on MI355X (gfx950): a decoder layer of a decode step as two persistent FlyDSL launches at TP8, opt-in with `--monokernel`. It is a standalone package, `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/mono/`, docked by `deepseek_v4/amd/mono_decode.py`, in the layout and style of the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash mono layer. No shared abstraction and no DeepSeek-V4.1 file is touched.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Release every prefill rank a READ holds
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fix three MoRIIO READ-mode bugs: prefill blocks left allocated after a fan-in read, a scrambled equal-TP read between different cache layouts, and a single-node xGMI crash in the flexible MLA mirror. Also add READ cases to the dummy-weight P/D E2E, and fix a port collision in that test. Follow-up to #61726. Split-head and Mamba READ across TP sizes is a separate PR stacked on this one.

## Claims

- **READ fan-in releases every prefill rank that holds the request.** Decode used to release only the rank it read from. With a larger prefill TP size, including the flexible MLA mirror (TP prefill + DP decode), the other prefill ranks kept the request's blocks until the `defer_timeout` reaper freed them: 60 s by default, logged as "Reaped N deferred sends".
- **Equal-TP READ between different cache layouts reads the right bytes.** Whole-block copies scrambled heads and tokens when prefill and decode lay them out differently. Such reads now move heads one by one. Matching layouts keep the same whole-block path.
- **Flexible MLA mirror on xGMI reads the fixed source.** The round-robin over prefill TP ranks spreads RDMA NIC load. On one node over xGMI it picked prefill ranks whose GPU MoRI cannot open a session to from a decode rank that sees one GPU ("MoRI could not open a session ... _tp1"). RDMA keeps the round-robin.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** new `tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_moriio_read_tp.py`, 93 tests. Each decode rank runs the real READ path on real cache tensors, and a fake transport executes the posted reads. The tests check that decode ends up byte-exact and that each prefill rank is released exactly as many times as it waits for. They cover:
  - equal TP for every fixture model × 3 cache-layout pairs
  - MLA in every TP pair, and replicated GQA at TP2 ↔ TP4
  - abort and failure releases
  - the RDMA round-robin vs the xGMI fixed source
- **The tests catch the bugs:** releasing only one holder fails 16 tests, and always copying whole blocks fails 12.
- **Full MoRIIO unit suite:** 818 passed. Ruff is clean, and mypy reports no new errors.
- **GPU, MI355X, xGMI:**

| Case (dummy-weight P/D) | Result |
|---|---|
| Equal-TP READ vs direct serve: kimi_linear, qwen3_5_moe, qwen3_dense, qwen3_dense HMA_off, deepseek_v3 HMA_off, gemma3 HMA_off | distance 0.0 on every prompt (ROCm 10; kimi_linear and qwen3_dense also on ROCm 7.2) |
| READ negative control (corrupted prefill KV): kimi_linear, qwen3_dense | detected |
| READ deepseek_v3 MLA, prefill TP1 → decode TP2 and TP2 → TP1 | pass, exact external hits. TP2 → TP1 crashed on main. |

## Details

- **Release accounting:** `get_moriio_read_holder_tp_ranks` lists the prefill ranks holding a decode rank's share. Decode releases all of them on completion, failure and abort, so prefill's existing `get_moriio_expected_ack_count` is met in both directions.
- **READ hit count in the E2E:** a READ decode always computes the last prompt token itself, so it reports `len − 1` external hits per prompt.
- **Port collisions in the E2E:** every TP rank binds the configured MoRIIO handshake and notify port plus its rank offset, and vLLM scans upward from each server's `VLLM_PORT`. The test handed out single ports, so a TP > 1 server's later ranks could land on another server's ports (`ZMQError: Address already in use`). This also affected #61726's heterogeneous WRITE cases. The test now reserves blocks of free ports.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Fix the Domyn Edge (ROCm) and Qwen2 embed HF references
commits.pr_body:
- `test_common.py`: on ROCm, generate the HF reference for `domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base` with `use_cache=False`
- `test_embedding.py`: keep the `ssmits/Qwen2-7B-Instruct-embed-base` HF reference on plain text with mean pooling

`test_models[...domyn/Domyn-Edge-Base]` has failed on MI355 since the model was added in #62544 ([build 96933](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96933/list?jid=01a16a2d-3c10-49ad-af03-b262a50862bd&tab=output)). vLLM's output is correct; it is the HF reference that turns to garbage after the first token. Domyn's remote code decodes through `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn`, and on ROCm that op aligns the causal mask to the top left when `max_q < max_k`, so with a KV cache every decode step only sees the first key. Recomputing without the cache keeps `max_q == max_k`, where the ROCm kernel is correct, so vLLM's Domyn coverage on ROCm stays in place. The PyTorch fix is pytorch/pytorch#201930; this part can be dropped once it is in the ROCm image.

The embedding test for `ssmits/Qwen2-7B-Instruct-embed-base` has failed on the CPU pooling job since #62835 bumped sentence-transformers to 5.6 ([build 97015](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97015)), with cosine 0.7963. That checkpoint has no sentence-transformers config, and 5.6 now wraps plain text in the tokenizer's chat template and uses last-token pooling for causal LMs, while the test pins vLLM to mean pooling of the plain text. Removing the `"message"` modality and putting a mean `Pooling` back gives the 5.2 embeddings again, and on older versions it is a no-op.

On MI350X with torch 2.12 and the CI pin 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0, `varlen_attn` with `window_size=(-1, 0)` and 1 query against 40 keys matches a top-left reference exactly, and the HF Domyn reference produces `' ItOlimpiadiOlimpiadi...'` with the KV cache and `' It is designed to run large language models (LLMs) on a wide range'` without it. For the embedding model, sentence-transformers 5.2.0 and 5.6.0 differ by exactly cosine 0.7963 on the same input; with this change, the reference from `HfRunner` under 5.6.0 matches 5.2.0 at cosine >= 0.999999 on all 8 example prompts.

## Overview

Streaming chat now drops tool calls in the same cases batch does. Fixes #63346. Follow-up to #63148 which listed this as not covered.

#42752 fixed #42747 for `"none"` but only inside `DelegatingParser`. Two cases still slip through on main:

- gpt-oss with `"none"`: `HarmonyParser` isn't a `DelegatingParser` so the guard never runs.
- `null` with any parser: nothing gates it, so streaming keeps tool calls while batch drops them.

This PR moves the rule into one place that batch and streaming both call, so it no longer depends on each parser.

## Claims

- With `stream: true`, `/v1/chat/completions` now follows the same `tool_choice` rules as batch. gpt-oss (Harmony) with `"none"` and any tool parser with `null` stop returning tool calls. This PR doesn't decide what `null` should mean, it only makes streaming match batch.
- Streaming `/v1/chat/completions/derender` gets the same fix because it uses the same `ChatStreamProcessor`.
- `finish_reason` is `stop` in those cases, not `tool_calls`.
- No change for `"auto"`, `"required"` or named tools. Anthropic and Cohere turn `null` into `"auto"` when tools are set, so they're not affected.

```text
  chat batch           tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  chat stream          tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender batch       tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
  derender stream      tool_calls=[]               finish=stop
```

The `auto` control still streams the tool call which means nothing extra is dropped.

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_stream_processor.py \
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_message_assembly.py \
tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_stream.py \
tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py \
tests/tool_use/mistral/test_mistral_tool_calls.py -v
```

New and changed tests:

- `test_drops_tool_calls_like_non_streaming`: `"none"` and `null`, with a mixed content and tool call delta and a tool call only delta.
- `test_e2e_harmony_tool_choice_none_drops_tool_calls`: now also runs with `stream: true` against the real gpt-oss render server.
- `test_derender_stream.py`: the `_FakeParser` fixture now has auto tools on. One test sent no tools with the default `tool_choice: "none"` and still expected tool calls, so it relied on this bug. It now sends `"auto"`.

No model eval. Generation doesn't change, only which parsed fields are returned.

No docs change. `tool_calling.md` already says `"none"` returns no tool calls.

## Details

`ChatStreamProcessor` passed `parse_delta()` output straight through and relied on the parser to check `tool_choice`. Not every parser does. `HarmonyParser` ignores `"none"` and the base `Parser` treats `null` like `"auto"`. Non-streaming doesn't have this problem because `assemble_chat_message_fields()` applies the rule itself.

The rule now lives in `keeps_tool_calls()` and both paths call it. `ChatStreamProcessor` takes `enable_auto_tools` and `parser_cls` as required keyword arguments, so a new caller can't skip them by accident.

When tool calls are dropped, the stream sends nothing for them. That matches batch which returns `content: ""`. Whether `"none"` should return tool-call-shaped text as content is #55080 and this PR doesn't change that. If a delta is empty after stripping, the processor returns `None`. Both callers already skip sending a `None` delta, the same way they handle hidden reasoning.

## Related PRs

- #42752 (merged): gates `"none"` in `DelegatingParser` only. This PR covers what that misses.
- #42868: targets the old `serving.py` streaming code which has since moved to `ChatStreamProcessor`. Obsolete and conflicting.
- #55089 / #55080: whether tool-call-shaped text should come back as content when tools are off. Out of scope here.
- #54321: makes an explicit `null` behave like an omitted field, so `"auto"` when tools are set. Complementary to this PR. If it lands, both paths follow it.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Multimodal] Make encoder cache free linear in items per request
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #54284. `EncoderCacheManager.free_encoder_input` scans all of a request's other cached inputs on every call, so freeing a request with N multimodal items is O(N²) on the scheduler thread. This makes it O(N) with the same release semantics.

## Claims

- Freeing a request with N multimodal items is now linear in N: 1,024 items drops from 15.9 ms to 0.29 ms, and 4,096 from 235 ms to 1.2 ms.
- No behaviour change: an entry is still held until the request's last occurrence of that `mm_hash` is freed, as #54284 requires.
- Only matters for prompts with hundreds of items (the default limit is 999 per modality). Typical prompts see under 0.1 ms difference.

## Validation

`EncoderCacheManager.free(request)` timed on `main` vs this PR: 5 runs, median in ms, CPU only (CPython 3.12).

| Items per request | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| 256 | 1.36 | 0.09 |
| 1,024 | 15.87 | 0.29 |
| 4,096 | 234.64 | 1.21 |

`pytest tests/v1/core/test_encoder_cache_manager.py`: 22 passed (21 existing, including the duplicate-hash tests from #54284, plus 1 new). CI runs the file through `pytest -m cpu_test v1/core`.

I did not do a GPU end-to-end run. This only changes scheduler bookkeeping, so model outputs are unaffected.

## Details

The `any(...)` check added in #54284 runs on every free, so freeing N inputs costs N(N−1)/2 comparisons on the engine-core thread, and the whole batch waits. This PR keeps `request_hash_refs[req_id][mm_hash]`, a count of the request's cached input ids per hash, updated where `request_cached_ids` changes. The check becomes a dict lookup.

Tradeoff: one small dict per request. An out-of-tree manager that subclasses `EncoderCacheManager` and writes `request_cached_ids` directly would also need to update `request_hash_refs`.

## Overview

Raise dependency minimums, including Sentence Transformers 5.6.0, regenerate the four compiled test requirement files, and require LMCache 0.5.6 for both CUDA connector variants. Certificate remediation is isolated in #62868; #59667 remains the separate automation change.

- Raise Sentence Transformers test minimums to 5.6.0 for CUDA, ROCm and nightly tests; pin XPU and all four compiled test locks to 5.6.0.
- Preserve unrelated pins. Certifi and OS certificate changes are excluded from this PR, allowing the certificate fix to proceed independently of LMCache compatibility validation.

## Validation

### Sentence Transformers 5.6.0 validation

- Regenerated CPU, CUDA, ROCm and XPU locks with uv 0.11.1 using their checked-in commands, preserving unrelated package versions. All applicable pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` passed.
- Existing pooling-config/schema tests: **6 passed**. Existing pooler activation tests: **25 passed**. Commands below ran in an isolated environment with Sentence Transformers 5.6.0, PyTorch 2.14.0 and Transformers 5.16.1.
- CPU compatibility smoke: seeded, two-layer tiny BERT with mean pooling, a dense projection and normalization; five inputs including one truncated input, plus three BERT CrossEncoder pairs. Using identical saved weights, 5.2.0 and 5.6.0 produced bit-identical embeddings and scores (maximum absolute difference **0**). Loading a 5.2.0 model under 5.6.0, saving/reloading under 5.6.0, and vLLM pooling/dense config parsing passed. ### Earlier dependency validation

- Regenerated locks with uv 0.11.1 and the exact configured platform/backend/constraint/exclusion arguments. All applicable `pre_commit run --files <changed files>` hooks and `git diff --check` passed after the split. The unchanged documentation lock was also regenerated successfully.
- Existing local checks with updated packages: 30 image tests, 4 MCP tests, 9 HTTP tests, and 24 LMCache connector unit tests passed. Locked Cargo metadata and a standalone rustls client compile passed.

The old 16-bit helper is absent; the published IPC descriptor/transport code has no `pickle.loads` fallback. This does not validate native extension loading.

Direct `cargo check -p rustls` hit a Cargo feature-resolution panic; metadata resolution and the separate rustls client compile passed.

</details>

**Pending:** Linux GPU builds, LMCache native-extension/ABI and real multiprocess integration, Rust frontend integration, and model/serving evaluations. These were not run on this macOS host. Dependency resolution and connector unit tests do not establish native ABI compatibility.

## Details

Both source requirements and generated outputs are updated so regeneration retains patched minimums. LMCache's CUDA 12.9 wheels are published separately from the CUDA 13 PyPI build for Linux x86_64 and aarch64. Existing Docker/Buildkite installers select the CUDA-specific file and constrain the installed accelerator stack. LMCache 0.5.6 changes the multiprocess wire format: workers and servers must be upgraded together.

commits.pr_title: [Doc][Recipe] MiniMax-M3.1-Flash: DEP2 + DEP4 PD on GB200/GB300, 7-token FLASHINFER_TS DSpark on NVIDIA
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Update the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash recipe's NVIDIA prefill/decode setup to one DEP2 prefill + one DEP4 decode on GB200 and GB300, and switch the NVIDIA DSpark default to seven speculative tokens on the FlashInfer PrimiTS (`FLASHINFER_TS`) draft backend.

**Draft:** served and evaluated on GB300 with the public image (see Validation); GB200 and the B200/B300 single-node smoke test are still pending.

## Claims

- **Guide:** "Prefill/decode disaggregation (1P1D, DEP2 + DEP4, NVIDIA GB200 / GB300)" replaces the GB200 TP4 + TP4 section. A DEP2 prefill on one tray feeds a DEP4 decode on a second tray. Both roles run DeepGEMM NVFP4 MegaMoE over expert parallelism, the V2 model runner and `--numa-bind`, with NIXL `engine_ttl: 0` and `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600`. The decode adds `--watermark 0.05`, 28 seqs per rank and FULL_DECODE_ONLY graphs up to 224 tokens. Host KV offload on the prefill is documented as an option.
- **Command builder:** `strategy_overrides.pd_cluster` renders the same pools and role flags for `gb200` / `gb300`. `vllm-router` is pinned to `--intra-node-data-parallel-size 1`, because it takes one DP size for both pools.
- **DSpark on NVIDIA (B200, B300, GB200, GB300):** `num_speculative_tokens` 3 → 7 and draft attention `FLASH_ATTN` → `FLASHINFER_TS`, in the feature and in the single-node GB200 guide command. AMD (3 tokens, `TRITON_ATTN`) and Hopper (no DSpark) are unchanged.

## Validation

- `node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes` passes on vllm-project/recipes `main` (6027ec8).
- Rendered commands checked:
  - `pd_cluster` on `gb200` / `gb300` renders DEP2 + DEP4 with the flags above.
  - Every NVIDIA rendering carries the 7-token `FLASHINFER_TS` draft.
  - MI355X renders unchanged, as do the B200 and B300 `pd_cluster` layouts and the non-`pd_cluster` GB200/GB300 layouts, apart from the draft.
- `pre-commit run --files recipes/models/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash.yaml` passes.
- **Served on GB300 (4-GPU trays) with `vllm/vllm-openai:minimax-m31-flash`** (arm64 `sha256:5d76347628973fb80519a919a2f2740b6645b62cba3fe2bd87b25f111bd0e948`), checkpoint `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash@a60dfa7` with its built-in `dspark/` draft. The guide's commands were run as written; only `--port` and cluster NIC/cache env were added. Each run checked the engine's logged args (DP sizes, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, the 7-token `FLASHINFER_TS` draft, `--watermark`) before evaluating.
- **gsm8k:** 5-shot, chat completions, `chat_template_kwargs: {thinking_mode: disabled}`, temperature 0, `max_tokens` 2048, all 1319 questions at once. Acceptance length comes from the engine's `/metrics` spec-decode counters around the eval (decode node for P/D).

  | Command | gsm8k flexible / strict | Null answers / truncated | DSpark acceptance length (k=7) | Other |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | 1P1D DEP2 + DEP4 (guide P/D section) | 0.9189 / 0.9067 | 0 / 0 | 4.55 | passkey 9/9 at 7.9K / 30.9K / 96.2K prompt tokens × 3 depths; 0 NIXL errors, 0 decode preemptions |
  | Single node TP4 (guide single-node command) | 0.9242 / 0.9151 | 0 / 0 | 4.77 | — |
  | Reference: TP4, same weights and eval, pre-release builds (2 runs) | 0.9204-0.9227 / 0.9128-0.9166 | | | |

  The P/D run is within run-to-run noise of the references (gsm8k at T=0 has varied by about 1pt between repeated runs of one config).
- **Startup:** the first P/D attempt failed on a cold node. The prefill's API servers hit vLLM's 600 s default `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S` during JIT builds, CUDA graph capture and FlashInfer autotune, so both P/D roles now set it to 3600. With partly warm JIT caches the prefill still took about 9 minutes and the decode about 5 minutes to start. The limit only applies with data parallel (one API server per DP rank). The single-node TP4 command is unaffected.
- **Pending (blocks ready-for-review):**
  - [ ] The P/D commands on GB200.
  - [ ] Single-node TP4 smoke test with the 7-token `FLASHINFER_TS` draft on B200 or B300, and on GB200: the server starts, answers a chat request, and draft acceptance is nonzero.

## Details

- **Where the layout comes from:** it and the per-role settings were tuned in GB300 AgentX runs on a pre-release build. In those runs, DEP4 decode beat DEP8 per GPU at the same batch per rank. A second DEP2 prefill did not raise throughput, because decode was the bottleneck. That build used features not upstream (a NIXL push transfer mode and a Mooncake-backed prefix pool), plus synthetic acceptance for throughput. The recipe uses NIXL pull, real acceptance (`rejection_sample_method: block`) and the public image instead.
- **Decode sizing:**
  - `--watermark 0.05` makes extra requests wait in the queue instead of preempting running ones.
  - The decode's `--max-num-batched-tokens` stays at 8192, because a preempted request recomputes its context in chunks of that size while every DP rank runs eager steps.
  - NIXL `engine_ttl: 0` turns off idle remote-engine cleanup; with the default one-hour TTL, a decode crashed an hour after its prefill went away.
- **Removed:** the GB200 TP4 + TP4 section (eager prefill, decode `--max-num-batched-tokens 512`, `enforce_handshake_compat: false`). Both roles now share the attention and DSpark configs, which the NIXL compatibility hash covers, so the handshake check can stay on.
- **Tradeoff:** the renderer applies a feature's args per hardware, not per strategy. So the 7-token draft is now the default for every NVIDIA layout, including high-concurrency DEP serving, where a shorter draft can give more throughput. InferenceX's GB200/GB300 DEP4 aggregated lanes use 3 tokens.
- **Known renderer behavior:** for models that fit on one node, the static JSON API co-locates the two PD roles on one node, so `hw/gb{200,300}/strategies/pd_cluster.json` shows the DEP4 decode on `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2,3`. The interactive builder uses the recipe's per-role `nodes` (one tray each). The current recipe has the same co-location.
- **Not a duplicate:** #63232 (the `minimax-m31-flash` support branch) adds an earlier version of this file. No other open PR changes it.

commits.pr_body:
- Add a ROCm kernel-to-source map producer that reads the actual CMake/Ninja objects, including host uses, header dependencies, and embedded GPU architectures.
- Record HIPify provenance for generated sources and copied or renamed headers while leaving the original sources intact.
- Preserve the original vendor header and repository patch as dependencies of generated Torch headers.

NVIDIA image builds already export kernel source maps for the CI selector. ROCm needs the same ownership information, but its native build transforms CUDA sources and headers into HIP inputs. The map uses the retained compilation and dependency records to recover those original paths and refuses incomplete or unsupported builds. This supplies the source half of the companion native SDK recording path, allowing CI to join observed kernel names to repository changes without guessing ownership.

Companion: [ci-infra native recording and selection for both backends](https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/685). Its consumers should be deployed before enabling the new map and recorder producers.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA][MoE] Process reloaded weights of LoRA-wrapped MoE layers
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With LoRA enabled, a layerwise weight reload (`reload_weights` with checkpoint-format weights, as used for RL weight sync) skips the post-load processing of quantized MoE experts. This PR makes `FusedMoEModularMethod.process_weights_after_loading` delegate to the wrapped quant method.

## Claims

- After this change, reloading a LoRA-enabled MoE model whose quant method converts weights after loading (e.g. compressed-tensors W4A16) gives the same base and adapter outputs as before the reload. On main the reload fails with a shape mismatch. If a kernel layout has the same shapes as the checkpoint, checkpoint-format tensors can instead stay in place silently.
- When the wrapped method builds a new kernel, the new experts and prepare/finalize receive the existing LoRA context, and the LoRA layer keeps using the same `FusedMoEKernel` object. If the new object cannot take the context, this fails instead of dropping the context silently. The test below does not cover this part (see Validation).
- Methods that keep their kernel on reload (e.g. unquantized) behave as before.

## Validation

Test `test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe` in `tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py` (CUDA only), on `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-quantized.w4a16` (compressed-tensors WNA16 MoE, `TritonWNA16Experts` on GB300), in eager mode:
- start the model with LoRA and record prompt logprobs, without an adapter and with `jeeejeee/qwen3-moe-text2sql-spider`;
- check that the adapter changes the logprobs;
- reload the model's own checkpoint;
- re-request the adapter, which the reload removed, and check that both logprob lists are exactly unchanged.

The test sets `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. Without it, repeating the same request in one process changed prompt logprobs by up to 3.0 (mean 0.2 to 0.4), so an exact comparison would be flaky. Expert names are sent in the LoRA-wrapped form (`experts.N.down_proj.base_layer.weight`), which is what `RoutedExperts` matches once LoRA has wrapped the layer. Eager mode makes sure the logprobs after the reload come from the rebuilt kernel.

```bash
pytest -v tests/model_executor/model_loader/test_reload.py::test_reload_weights_with_lora_moe
```

Run on 1x GB300 with the nightly image at `8e2beaa3bf`, which is older than this PR's base. These files are the same in both: `fused_moe_modular_method.py`, `vllm/lora/layers/fused_moe.py`, `vllm/model_executor/model_loader/reload/`, and the base version of `test_reload.py`.

| `fused_moe_modular_method.py` | Result |
|---|---|
| base | FAILED: `The size of tensor a (1024) must match the size of tensor b (256) at non-singleton dimension 2` |
| this PR | PASSED |
| this PR without the LoRA-context transfer | PASSED |

What the test does not cover: the LoRA-context transfer. Without it, an instrumented run showed that after the reload all 48 MoE layers run the rebuilt `TritonWNA16Experts` with no LoRA context, which skips the expert LoRA. Even so, the adapter's logprobs matched the pre-reload values exactly. I have not found out why the expert part of this adapter has no visible effect in this setup, so the transfer is kept based on the code path (`TritonExperts`, `MarlinExperts` and the TRT-LLM LoRA experts read `_lora_context` in `apply`), not on a test.

I did not extend `test_reload_weights` instead. Its MoE cases are DeepSeek-V3 debug checkpoints, and with LoRA enabled, a checkpoint-format reload of those fails before reaching this code, in `DeepseekV2` weight loading (`KeyError: 'layers.0.mlp.gate.e_score_correction_bias'`, because the LoRA-wrapped gate's parameters are named `gate.base_layer.*`). This happens on main too and is not changed here.

The test is not marked `slow_test`, so the H200 Model Executor step selects it. It loads a ~16 GB checkpoint and a ~1.7 GB adapter.

`pre-commit` hooks `ruff-check`, `ruff-format`, `check-forbidden-imports` and `mypy` (Python 3.11) pass on the changed files.

Other checks, outside the test:
- **Different checkpoint state:** I reloaded a copy of the checkpoint with expert scales perturbed, back and forth, with CUDA graphs on and off. After returning to the original weights, base and adapter prompt logprobs matched a cold start within run-to-run noise. This is the same result as reloading the same weights.
- **Reload to the perturbed state:** after this reload, outputs differed from a cold start of the perturbed checkpoint (mean |Δlogprob| ≈ 0.5, against a noise level of ≈ 0.06). The expert parameters were equal to the cold start. The same difference appears **without LoRA**, so it is not caused by this change.
- **Kernel-format reload:** a checkpoint reload followed by a kernel-format reload (`is_checkpoint_format=False`) gives wrong outputs in eager mode. Rebuilt kernels keep references to the temporary tensors from the checkpoint reload. With CUDA graphs the outputs are correct. This also happens **without LoRA**, where the unwrapped method rebuilds its kernel the same way.

Not run: an end-to-end RL weight sync on this head, NVFP4 or other backends in the test (no NVFP4 MoE backend supports batch-invariant mode), and EP/DP.

## Details

Root cause: `FusedMoEWithLoRA` replaces the experts' quant method with `FusedMoEModularMethod`, which wraps the original method and holds the kernel that the LoRA layer also holds. The wrapper does not override `process_weights_after_loading`, so it is the base no-op. On the first load this does not matter, because the wrapper is installed after processing. On a layerwise reload, the reload code calls the wrapper's no-op and then copies the unprocessed checkpoint-format tensors into the kernel tensors.

Fix: the wrapper calls the wrapped method's `process_weights_after_loading`. Most quantized methods build a new kernel there. In that case the wrapper:
- passes the LoRA context of the current experts and prepare/finalize to the new ones (the LoRA layer sets it only once, at creation),
- puts the new kernel's `impl` into the existing `FusedMoEKernel`,
- points the wrapped method at that kernel and refreshes `moe_quant_config`.

This follows what the unwrapped method does on reload. The kernel-format reload issue above, and graph-captured tensors that belong to replaced experts (e.g. the TRT-LLM MXFP4 experts' `gemm1_alpha`), apply to that shared rebuild-on-reload behaviour as well. For GPT-OSS with LoRA, the reload fails before processing, in the model's weight-name mapping (`KeyError: 'layers.0.mlp.experts.w2_bias'`).

A side note, not changed here: when the checkpoint names of expert weights do not have the `base_layer.` part, the weights of LoRA-wrapped experts are skipped during a reload. A warning (`RoutedExperts: Failed to load weights`) is logged and no error is raised.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Remap invalid topk_ids in moe_permute without expert_map
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #59686. `moe_permute` returns wrong `expert_first_token_offset` when `topk_ids` contains `-1` (the id the router writes for CUDA-graph padding tokens with `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING=1`, the default) and no `expert_map` is given. The CUTLASS fp8 MoE path then runs some valid tokens through the wrong expert. This always applies the existing invalid-id remap in `moe_sort_routing`.

## Claims

- Valid tokens' MoE outputs no longer depend on CUDA-graph padding when `CutlassExpertsFp8` (and the other `moe_permute` callers: `cutlass_moe.py` W4A8 path, Humming non-scatter path) run without an `expert_map`.
- Fixes single-request serving quality of fp8 MoE checkpoints on the auto-selected `VLLM_CUTLASS` backend (first-token collapse to `'\n'`, off-topic sampled output).
- No change when all ids are valid or when an `expert_map` is given (the remap already ran there).

## Validation

H100 (SM 9.0), vLLM `main` `47de9d4d04`, `_moe_C_stable_libtorch` rebuilt for sm_90 with CUDA 13.1; unpatched = the precompiled nightly extension for the same source.

| check | unpatched | patched |
|---|---|---|
| repro from #59686: batch sizes (1..48, padded to a multiple of 8) with wrong offsets | 42 / 48 | 0 / 48 |
| `CutlassExpertsFp8` (E=128, top-4, K=3072, N=1536, per-token act / per-channel weight fp8): sizes where valid rows differ from an unpadded call | 25 / 48 | 0 / 48 |
| new `test_moe_permute_invalid_expert_ids_without_expert_map` | 8 failed (offset assertion) | 8 passed |
| `tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py` | | 462 passed |

Model evaluation, 128-expert top-4 fp8 MoE checkpoint (compressed-tensors `FP8_DYNAMIC`), TP=2, default backends (`VLLM_CUTLASS` MoE, CUDA graphs on). Next-token distributions vs. the bf16 checkpoint on 90 short chat prompts x thinking on/off; "foreign mass" = probability the fp8 model puts on its top-10 tokens that are outside the bf16 top-100 (0 for bf16 vs. itself).

| regime (first 8 response tokens) | unpatched: foreign mass / p99 / top-1 agreement | patched |
|---|---|---|
| greedy decode, one request at a time | 0.0081 / 0.39 / 0.951 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.988 |
| teacher-forced, one request at a time | 0.0028 / 0.0000 / 0.979 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.989 |
| teacher-forced, all requests in one batch | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.990 | 0.0000 / 0.0000 / 0.990 |

Commands:

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_permute_unpermute.py
```

## Details

Root cause: `CubKeyValueSorter` radix-sorts only the low `floor(log2(2E-1)) + 1` bits, so a raw `-1` (all ones) sorts after every real expert, but `findTotalEltsLessThanTarget` binary-searches the keys as signed ascending ints. Probes landing in the trailing `-1`s push offsets too high, so an expert's grouped-GEMM segment can cover the next expert's rows; when padding outnumbers valid tokens every offset equals the total route count and the valid MoE output is zero. `preprocessTopkIdKernel` already maps ids outside `[0, n_expert)` to the `n_expert` sentinel the sort expects, but it only ran with an `expert_map` or `build_inverse`; `moe_permute` / `moe_permute_with_scratch` pass neither on a single EP rank.

Cost: one `n_token * topk` int32 copy and one elementwise kernel per `moe_permute` call, no host sync, CUDA-graph safe.

`preprocessTopkIdLauncher` now returns early for an empty batch, since the unconditional call would otherwise compute `block = 0`. This overlaps #58790 (empty routing in `moe_permute`, open); whichever lands second can drop its guard.

Not duplicate: open PRs on the same `-1` padding sentinel target other backends (AITER #57036, FlashInfer b12x #57946, XPU #55231) or empty routing (#58790); none changes the `moe_sort_routing` remap gate. Searched `moe_permute`, `expert_first_token_offset`, `topk_ids -1 padding`, `VLLM_MOE_SKIP_PADDING`, `preprocessTopkId`.

Limitations: validated on H100 only; the sm_90 kernel build used CUDA 13.1.

AI assistance: Claude Code was used to localize the bug, write the repros, the fix and the test, and run the validation. The human submitter reviewed every changed line and the results.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Validate gfx942's int4 expert requant as int4
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Since #59042, Kimi-K3 with `--quantization-config '{"moe": {"weight": "int4_per_group_32"}}'` fails at startup on gfx942. This PR changes the fail-closed MoE experts check so it validates gfx942's load-time int4 requant as int4.

## Claims

- Kimi-K3 with the int4 expert requant starts and serves on gfx942 again.
- MXFP4 backend selection is unchanged for every other model and GPU.

## Validation

All runs on 8x MI325X (gfx942).

- **Before:** `upstream/main` (`87b804f09d`) fails in `Mxfp4MoEMethod._setup_kernel_k3_situ_gfx942`. I reproduced it by calling `_validate_mxfp4_experts_config(AiterMxfp4Experts, <K3 SiTU MoE config>, AITER_MXFP4_BF16)` on the device:
  ```
  ValueError: AiterMxfp4Experts does not support this MoE deployment since kernel does not support quantization scheme QuantKey(u8,scale(u8,static,GroupShape(row=1, col=32)),symmetric)xNone.
  ```
  With this change the same call passes.
- **Serving:** `vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 -tp 8 --quantization-config '{"moe":{"weight":"int4_per_group_32"}}'`, with DSpark (k=7) and stock decode.
  - The server starts, requantizes the experts, logs `Using AiterMxfp4Experts`, and runs AITER's `flydsl_moe*_abf16_wint4` kernels.
  - GSM8K (5-shot, 1319 questions, concurrency 1) scores 0.9575 ± 0.0056 on both strict and flexible extract.
- **Tests:** two new tests in `tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py`. Both fake the arch, so any ROCm CI machine covers every arch.
  - `test_aiter_mxfp4_experts_quant_scheme_support_by_arch`: `AiterMxfp4Experts` accepts MXFP4 on gfx950 only and int4 on gfx942 only.
  - `test_mxfp4_experts_check_accepts_aiter_deployments`: the fail-closed check accepts every AITER MXFP4 backend on each arch it is deployed on, plus the gfx942 Kimi-K3 int4 requant.
  - `pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_rocm_aiter_moe.py -k "quant_scheme_support or check_accepts_aiter"` gives 13 passed. On `upstream/main`, exactly the two gfx942 int4 cases fail (2 failed, 11 passed), one with the `ValueError` above.
  - `pytest tests/models/kimi_k3/test_gfx942_int4.py` gives 7 passed.

## Details

- **Root cause:** #51274 requantizes K3's MXFP4 experts to packed int4 (`kInt4Static32`, bf16 activations) on gfx942. It builds the kernel with `make_mxfp4_moe_kernel(experts_cls=AiterMxfp4Experts)`.
  - #59042, a CUTLASS FP4 expert-parallel fix, added `_validate_mxfp4_experts_config` at the top of that shared function. The check validates an experts class with the first of `_MXFP4_SCHEME_CANDIDATES` the class supports. If none match, it falls back to the MXFP4 keys.
  - The AITER experts accept MXFP4 keys on gfx950 only. #60322 kept that rule when it split `AiterExperts` into per-quant classes.
  - So on gfx942 no candidate matched, and the check rejected the int4 experts.
- **Fix:** `AiterMxfp4Experts` accepts `(kInt4Static32, None)` on gfx942 only, and that pair is appended as the last candidate.
  - The oracle's backend selection passes `kMxfp4Static` explicitly, so it is unaffected.
  - Classes that support an MXFP4 key still pick that key first, so gfx950 is unchanged.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to develop this change. I reviewed every changed line and ran the tests above.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][LoRA] Don't reject LoRA for speculative decoding drafters
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #61884. `LoRAConfig.verify_with_model_config` now skips the `SupportsLoRA` check for speculative decoding drafters (`runner_type == "draft"`), so LoRA + spec decode works again with drafters that don't implement `SupportsLoRA`. Reported by @cjackal in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61884#issuecomment-6346398560 and the following comments.

## Claims

- With `enable_lora` and a drafter without `SupportsLoRA` (e.g. `DeepSeekMTPModel`), the draft `VllmConfig` validates again instead of raising `LoRA is not supported for ...`.
- Target models without `SupportsLoRA` (e.g. Zamba2) are still rejected at config time, as in #61884.
- No change for drafters that implement `SupportsLoRA` (e.g. EAGLE-Llama, Llama draft models).

## Validation

CPU reproduction: `EngineArgs(model="luccafong/deepseek_mtp_main_random", enable_lora=True, speculative_config={"method": "mtp", "num_speculative_tokens": 1}).create_engine_config()`, then `replace(cfg, model_config=cfg.speculative_config.draft_model_config)`, as `DraftModelProposer` and other proposers do:

| | main @ `71e9320633` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| target `DeepseekV3ForCausalLM` (`SupportsLoRA`) | OK | OK |
| draft `DeepSeekMTPModel` (`runner_type="draft"`, no `SupportsLoRA`) | `ValidationError` from the LoRA check | OK |

Tests:

```bash
pytest tests/test_config.py -k lora
```

- New `test_lora_allowed_for_drafter_without_lora_support`; the existing #61884 test now sets `runner_type="generate"` and still checks the rejection.
- Full `tests/test_config.py`: 438 passed. The same 14 tests fail on main and on this branch, all on Hugging Face downloads (gated or unavailable models in my environment).
- `pre-commit run` on the changed files passes.

Validated on CPU only; I did not run LoRA + spec decode end to end on a GPU.

## Details

**Root cause:** `VllmConfig.__post_init__` calls `lora_config.verify_with_model_config(self.model_config)`. Several proposers rebuild the `VllmConfig` with the draft model config via `dataclasses.replace` (e.g. `DraftModelProposer`, Step-3.5, the MRV2 standalone/Gemma4 speculators, Qwen4Exp/Step5 MTP), so the check from #61884 also ran on the drafter.

**Fix:** skip the check when `model_config.runner_type == "draft"`. LoRA is only applied to the target model (`load_lora_model` wraps `self.model` in the model runners), so drafters don't need `SupportsLoRA`.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][RDNA][Perf] W4A16: packed fp16 prefill dequant and tiles for gfx1151
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Speeds up fp16 prefill in `RDNAHybridW4A16LinearKernel` on gfx1151 (Strix Halo). The Triton prefill GEMM dequantizes two 4-bit weights per instruction, and gets tiles tuned for that dequant. Supersedes draft #55711.

## Claims

- fp16 prefill latency on gfx1151: 5–18% faster on Qwen3-4B (symmetric) at every prompt length from 64 to 2048 tokens, and 17–19% faster on Qwen3-8B (asymmetric) from 512 tokens, unchanged below.
- No change for bf16, or on any GPU other than gfx1151.
- No accuracy change: the dequant arithmetic is exact, and kernel output is bit-identical to main in all 1248 configs swept.

## Validation

All measurements: gfx1151 (Radeon 8060S), torch 2.13.0+rocm10.2, Triton 3.8.0. main is c83935b300. Benchmarks ran on 23a1a2b640, which differs from this PR's head only in comments and in where `packed_dequant` is decided (same result for every dtype, zero-point and M). GSM8K and tests ran on the head.

**End-to-end prefill latency**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size 1 --output-len 1 --num-iters-warmup 5 --num-iters 30 --max-model-len 4096 --seed 0`. One process per run, main and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is main → this PR, median over reps in ms, with the delta; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B, fp16, sym | Qwen3-8B, fp16, asym | Qwen3-8B, bf16, asym (control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 34.9 → 33.0 (−5.4%) | 71.1 → 71.6 (+0.7% ~) | 74.1 → 74.2 (+0.2% ~) |
| 128 | 51.5 → 46.7 (−9.4%) | 92.2 → 92.5 (+0.3% ~) | 96.3 → 96.2 (−0.2% ~) |
| 192 | 76.5 → 72.6 (−5.1%) | 140.9 → 140.3 (−0.4% ~) | 147.9 → 148.0 (+0.0% ~) |
| 256 | 91.1 → 76.5 (−16.0%) | 165.0 → 163.1 (−1.1%) | 174.8 → 172.8 (−1.1% ~) |
| 512 | 175.7 → 144.3 (−17.9%) | 325.7 → 264.5 (−18.8%) | 340.6 → 342.1 (+0.4% ~) |
| 2048 | 782.7 → 673.5 (−14.0%) | 1346.3 → 1118.8 (−16.9%) | 1366.0 → 1364.8 (−0.1% ~) |

**Large batches**: `vllm bench latency --batch-size {128,256} --output-len {1,128} --num-iters-warmup 1 --num-iters 1 --max-model-len 4096 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 256 --seed 0`. One process per run, main (11a8d571d2, this PR's parent) and this PR alternating, 3 reps. Each cell is the change in end-to-end latency from main, median over reps; "~" marks overlapping rep ranges.

| batch | prompt tokens | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 1 | Qwen3-4B fp16 sym, output 128 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 1 | Qwen3-8B fp16 asym, output 128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 128 | −47.8% | −26.3% | −51.8% | −28.6% |
| 128 | 256 | −47.2% | −30.9% | −51.9% | −34.8% |
| 128 | 512 | −47.6% | −34.6% | −51.4% | −40.3% |
| 128 | 1024 | −46.9% | −36.1% | −51.1% | −43.0% |
| 256 | 128 | −48.0% | −29.2% | −51.8% | −29.7% |
| 256 | 256 | −48.0% | −32.7% | −51.7% | −36.1% |
| 256 | 512 | −47.8% | −35.6% | −51.6% | −41.0% |

Qwen3-8B bf16 (control, prompt 512): batch 128 +2.9% ~ at output 1 and −0.1% ~ at output 128; batch 256 −0.5% ~ and +0.4% ~.

Models are `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` and `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16`.

**Accuracy**: GSM8K, 5-shot, 500 questions, greedy, `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` against a server started with `--dtype float16 --max-model-len 4096`. Differences are ±1 question.

| model | dtype | quant | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | asym | 0.884 | 0.882 |
| `RedHatAI/Qwen3-4B-quantized.w4a16` | fp16 | sym | 0.848 | 0.850 |

**Tests**: 135 passed on gfx1151. CI has no gfx11 runners: the AMD kernel quantization shards run on MI300/MI355, where these tests skip.

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py \
       tests/kernels/quantization/test_w4a16_kernel_selection.py
```

<details>
<summary>Kernel sweep</summary>

Calls `_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply_impl` directly with the main and PR copies of `rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py`, timed with `triton.testing.do_bench` and a cache flush between reps, as in `benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_rdna_hybrid_w4a16_gemm.py`. Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-1.7B qkv/o/gate_up/down shapes, group size 32/64/128, M 6–2048, 1248 configs, 3 reps with rotating order. Geomean kernel time vs main; lower is better.

| dtype | quant | M | Qwen3-8B | Qwen3-1.7B |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fp16 | sym | ≤ 128 | 0.972 | 0.979 |
| fp16 | sym | 129–256 | 0.845 | 0.968 |
| fp16 | sym | > 256 | 0.762 | 0.787 |
| fp16 | asym | ≤ 128 | 0.999 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | 129–256 | 0.996 | 0.999 |
| fp16 | asym | > 256 | 0.766 | 0.795 |
| bf16 | sym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 0.999–1.000 |
| bf16 | asym | all | 0.997–1.000 | 1.000 |

Output bit-identical to main: 1248 of 1248 configs.

Geomeans hide some per-shape losses for symmetric fp16: 46 of its 312 configs are more than 2% slower than main (195 are more than 2% faster). The worst is Qwen3-1.7B `down_proj` (K = 6144, N = 2048) at M = 129–192, 13–22% slower. Every loss was already present in #55711.

</details>

## Details

**Packed dequant.** For a 4-bit value `n`, the bits `0x6400 | n` read as fp16 are exactly `1024 + n`. One `v_and_or_b32` (`(x & 0x000F000F) | 0x64006400`) does this for two values at once, instead of the `v_and_b16` + `v_or_b16` per value that Triton emits. The ExLlama shuffle layout already puts paired values 16 bits apart, so no extra shuffling is needed. The kernel subtracts `1024 + zp` instead of `zp`, which is exact because fp16 represents every integer below 2048.

**When it is used.** Only fp16 on gfx1151, the only GPU it was measured on, decided on the host and passed to the kernel as the `PACKED_DEQUANT` constexpr. Asymmetric layers use it only above M = 256: the extra zero-point load made it 1.2–2.4x slower per GEMM below that.

**Tiles.** The packed fp16 path and the scalar bf16 path want different tiles, most visibly `BLOCK_N` 256 vs 64 at deep M. `_select_skinny_gfx1151_config` picks new tiles and `num_stages=1` for fp16 above M = 128 (M = 256 for asymmetric). Everything else keeps the existing ladder and overrides unchanged. `num_stages=1` stays off bf16, where it cost 15.8% end-to-end on an asymmetric model.

**Numerics.** The dequant result is unchanged. The new tiles change `BLOCK_K`, and with it the fp32 accumulation order, so fp16 output is not guaranteed bit-identical. In the kernel sweep it was bit-identical in all 1248 configs.

**Not duplicating.** #57199 changes the HIP decode kernel, not the Triton prefill path. #52637 changes symmetric weight loading in `process_weights_after_loading`. #60710 adds an opt-in (default off) dense weight cache that skips the int4 dequant at M ≥ 256; it edits the same file but leaves the Triton dequant and tile selection alone. commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Fix cooperative_topk illegal memory access on NaN scores
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Since #59645, `cooperative_topk` crashes with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` when a row of 64K columns or more contains more NaNs than `top_k` (e.g. 1% of a 256K row, or a fully-NaN row). NaN scores can reach decode top-k during warmup and CUDA-graph capture, where the indexer reads uninitialized KV blocks (see the note in `candidate_blocks.py`). Before #59645 such rows produced garbage indices; now they take down the process.

**Root cause.** nvcc compiles the integer expression `bits | 0x80000000u` in `convert_to_uint32_v2` as the FP operation `-|x|`:

```
ISETP.GE.AND P0, PT, R2, RZ        // bits >= 0 ?
FADD R10, -|R2|, -RZ               // "bits | 0x80000000u" emitted as -|x|
@P0 IMAD.MOV.U32 R9, RZ, RZ, R10
```

That is bit-exact for finite values and ±inf, but FADD canonicalizes NaN to `0x7FFFFFFF`, which is the ordered key of -0.0. The FP16 coarse bins put NaN above +inf (bin 1023), so the two orderings disagree. When NaNs overflow the threshold bin, the exact recovery takes the single-key path with a -0.0 pivot. Every positive score then counts as "above" it, and the unchecked append in `collect_exact_candidates` writes past `s_topk` (compute-sanitizer: invalid `__shared__` write in `unbounded_round0_single_key`).

**Fix.** Read the bits through an opaque `mov.b32`, so the key stays bit-exact and NaN orders above +inf in both the coarse and exact keys, matching `torch.topk`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Don't count adaptive verification profiling cache as CUDA graph memory
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With adaptive verification on, Model Runner V2 counts the allocator cache left by adaptive verification's cost-profiling dummy runs as CUDA graph memory, and takes it from the KV cache. This PR releases that cache before `capture_model` takes its closing memory reading.

## Claims

- Fixes the over-counted CUDA graph memory under adaptive verification, in both the memory-profiling estimate pass and the real capture (0.92 → 0.07 GiB in the run below). The KV cache gets that memory back.
- When KV capacity is the bottleneck, decode throughput recovers: 40.5 → 113.2 tok/s in the run below, matching the same config without adaptive verification (110.2 tok/s).
- Startup only. Nothing changes in steady-state execution, and runs without adaptive verification are unaffected.

## Validation

**Startup log.** 1× L4, `Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct` with `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` as `draft_model`, `num_speculative_tokens=4`, `enable_adaptive_verification=true`, `TRITON_ATTN`, `max_model_len=32768`, `max_num_seqs=3`, prefix caching on:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 3 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.36 \
  --speculative-config '{"method": "draft_model", "model": "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    "num_speculative_tokens": 4, "enable_adaptive_verification": true}'
# compare the two "Graph capturing finished ... took X GiB" lines and "GPU KV cache size"
```

**Throughput.** Decode-bound long-context workload, greedy, `max_tokens=256`:
- 12 prompts, each a 24K-token slice of vLLM's docs followed by a question.
- Contexts are processed in groups of 3. Each group is first prefilled with one question, then timed with a different question, so the timed requests reuse the warmed prefix.
- One run per config. The memory numbers are deterministic: both runs without the fix logged 0.92 / 0.88 GiB.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | Config | "Graph capturing ... took" (estimate / real) | GPU KV cache | Prefix hit rate | Output tok/s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.36 | main, adaptive verification | 0.92 / 0.88 GiB | 64,688 tokens | 37.8% | 40.5 |
| 0.36 | this PR, adaptive verification | 0.07 / 0.04 GiB | 86,960 tokens | 50.0% | 113.2 |
| 0.36 | adaptive verification off (reference) | 0.07 / 0.03 GiB | 87,376 tokens | 50.0% | 110.2 |
| 0.9 | main, adaptive verification | 0.92 / 0.88 GiB | 376,432 tokens | 50.0% | 110.6 |
| 0.9 | this PR, adaptive verification | 0.07 / 0.04 GiB | 398,912 tokens | 50.0% | 110.1 |

At 0.36, 64,688 tokens can't hold three ~24.3K-token requests. Prefixes get evicted and re-prefilled (hit rate 37.8% vs 50%), and decode runs fewer requests at once. At 0.9 there's enough KV either way, so only the KV size changes.

The effect is larger with bigger models. With #60339's suffix speculator and adaptive verification on Qwen2.5-7B at 24K context (L4, utilization 0.9), the leftover cache was 1.88 GiB:
- KV cache: 44,400 tokens before, 79,584 after.
- Long-context decode: 0.28× of no speculation before, 1.39× after.

**Tests.**

```bash
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py tests/v1/spec_decode/test_adaptive_verification.py
# 48 passed
```

The new `test_capture_model_excludes_adaptive_verification_profiling_cache` covers both `profile_only=False` and `profile_only=True`, and fails on main.

## Details

**Root cause.** `capture_model` reads free memory, captures the graphs, then reads free memory again. The difference is reported as CUDA graph memory. When adaptive verification is on, the profiling for its cost curves also runs between those two readings: `batches_to_profile`, i.e. 5 replays of each capture size plus tail sizes up to `max_num_batched_tokens`, with the profiling context length. Those dummy runs free their tensors, but the caching allocator keeps the blocks. `get_memory_info` therefore sees them as used: about 0.85 GiB here, and 1.9 GiB with a 7B target (allocated delta ≈ 0, all of it reserved cache).

The same `capture_model` serves `profile_cudagraph_memory`'s estimate pass, whose result is subtracted from the KV budget. So the KV cache is sized as if graphs needed that memory.

**Fix.** Call `torch.accelerator.empty_cache()` after `set_initial_cost_curves`, matching the `empty_cache()` that already runs before the first reading. The profiling timings are already collected by then, since `StepTimingCollector.collect` synchronizes on exit.

**Scope.**
- Model Runner V1 has no adaptive verification.
- #52233 (opt-in persistent profile cache) touches the same block. On a cache hit it would skip the dummy runs, but it's off by default and doesn't change the accounting.
- #54065 and #54077 change the shapes of the profiled tail, not the memory accounting.

**Not duplicating existing work.** I searched open and closed PRs and issues for "empty_cache adaptive verification", "capture_model memory adaptive", "cuda graph memory adaptive verification", "adaptive verification KV cache memory" and "batches_to_profile". The only related results are the PRs listed under Scope.

- C1/N10 seed `210101`, C8/N80 seed `210108`, and C32/N320 seed `210132`.
- Both arms receive the same unique prompts. Every accepted run has zero prefix-cache hit tokens.

| Case | Baseline Input TPS | Candidate Input TPS | Candidate delta | Baseline Mean TTFT | Candidate Mean TTFT | Candidate delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| C1 / N10 | 13,933.06 | 21,994.20 | +57.86% | 587.75 ms | 372.25 ms | -36.66% |
| C8 / N80 | 14,240.95 | 22,866.70 | +60.57% | 4,399.97 ms | 2,739.59 ms | -37.74% |
| C32 / N320 | 14,252.14 | 22,894.56 | +60.64% | 17,499.31 ms | 10,890.08 ms | -37.77% |

All 820 requests across both arms succeeded. Decoder-side replay improves uncached 8K prefill throughput by 58-61% across C1-C32.

### Paired GSM8K accuracy

Full 1,319 samples, four-shot, batch 64, seed 42, temperature 0, top-p 1, reasoning effort `high`, and `max_tokens=8192`, using EvalScope 1.11.1:

| Arm | Correct | Accuracy | API errors | Max-token stops |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 1,286/1,319 | 97.498% | 0 | 0 |
| Candidate | 1,282/1,319 | 97.195% | 0 | 1 |

The arms used the same sample indexes, prompts, targets, and total input-token count. Paired outcomes were 1,278 both-correct, 29 both-wrong, 8 baseline-only correct, and 4 candidate-only correct. The exact two-sided McNemar test gives `p=0.387695`, so the observed 0.303 percentage-point difference is not statistically significant.

Both arms recorded exactly 674,816 / 803,206 local prefix-cache hit tokens (84.02%) and zero external cache-hit tokens. The sole candidate truncation was sample index 119, which reached 8,192 output tokens; the corresponding baseline request stopped normally at 6,955 output tokens.

Both service pods remained Ready with zero restarts. The performance and accuracy runs had zero API failures, and post-test logs contained no critical runtime, CUDA, or engine errors.

## Details

Reuse the existing replay batch, gather kernel and attention builders. Each PCP rank-local `InputBatch` carries compact PCP metadata: the unpadded global token count, per-segment global query and sequence-length bounds, and the PCP+DCP gather bound. Decoder replay derives local trailing rows and the same global kept-token padding bound on every rank without carrying the global batch or adding a PCP collective. Replay-start upload is deferred until PCP/DP agreement confirms replay is needed. Select local slots before compaction, gather them in rank-major order, and align MoE routing IDs with the compact rows. Batches that would not shrink after padding keep full execution.

Unlike #61554's APC-disabled cold-prefill path, this builds on #62183 for APC prefix hits and derives replay bounds from existing global PCP metadata. It retains the existing PCP restrictions and eager execution requirement, with no scheduler or configuration changes. The branch is rebased on #62183 now in main. commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Fix Triton paged decode leaving output heads unwritten on gfx942
commits.pr_body:
- `chunked_prefill_paged_decode.py`: offset the output pointer to the token's row as a 64-bit scalar and keep the per-head store offsets 32-bit.
- `test_prefix_prefill.py`: fill the output with NaN, so a row the kernel skips fails every time instead of passing on leftover memory.

`test_qwen3_nonstandard_block_size[True-chunked_prefill_paged_decode-...-8-4-256-1056]`, added with the interleaved V cache in #42755, fails on MI300 intermittently ([build 96693](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96693/list?jid=01a164e7-c489-4e2d-9709-6796df461d5f&tab=output)). Locally it fails 6 of 20 runs on main. The Triton decode kernel only writes 263 of the decode token's 2048 output values, so the result depends on whatever memory the output buffer reuses. The kernel's logic is correct: under `TRITON_INTERPRET=1`, or with `AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0`, every value is written. The LLVM IR computes the 64-bit head offset correctly, but in the gfx942 ISA the `output_stride_1` argument is never read and the head index is multiplied by an unrelated spilled SGPR instead (the block-table row offset, in the variant traced). Rows land at the wrong offsets, so most values are left unwritten and some heads overwrite others. This only happens in variants with hundreds of SGPR spills; computing the per-head offset in 32 bits avoids it, so the change is a workaround for a backend miscompile. The interleaved V path is not the only one affected: the normal layout loses outputs too, on the Triton fallback with 128 and 256 token pages at head size 128 and 256, which hybrid models with large pages can hit. On a decode-only sweep of 60 head-size, GQA, page-size and layout combinations, 18 dropped stores before this change and none after; kernel time changes by -0.4% to +1.4%.

commits.pr_title: [Core] Let VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS set the EngineCore cleanup grace after an immediate abort
commits.pr_body:
With the default `--shutdown-timeout 0`, the process manager sends EngineCore a SIGTERM and then kills it with SIGKILL straight away on every platform except ROCm, which gets 15 s since #52281. This PR lets an explicitly set `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` set that cleanup window on every platform. Defaults stay the same. This is the vLLM follow-up promised in vllm-project/ci-infra#685 ([review thread](https://github.com/vllm-project/ci-infra/pull/685#discussion_r4355552793)).

ci-infra#685 records the GPU kernels each CI process launches. A recording counts as complete only if it ends with a footer, which the CUPTI injection library writes from `atexit` and the ROCProfiler SDK tool writes from `tool_fini`. In CUDA build [vllm/ci 96247](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96247), 4,400 of 18,118 recordings had no footer. Matching them against the job logs, 540 are EngineCore processes killed right after `stopping engine client mode=abort timeout=0s`, and another 391 are TP/EP workers killed in the same process-tree kill. In the CPU offload job, for example, all 8 servers log `send sigterm` and `force killing remaining process EngineCore` within 1 ms of each other. EngineCore already handles SIGTERM by leaving its busy loop and exiting normally through `sys.exit` in the spawn bootstrap (`RemoteOpenAIServer` forces spawn), so all it needs is time.

`VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` is already documented as the "timeout in seconds for engine and worker process shutdown", and the client finalizer already uses it to shut down the EngineCore process manager, so this PR adds no new knob. Making the grace opt-in keeps the fast CUDA shutdown default unchanged. A user who sets the variable on ROCm now gets that value instead of the fixed 15 s. The kernel recorder exports `=30` on recording runs (ROCm today, and CUDA with vllm-project/ci-infra#685).

- `get_engine_process_shutdown_timeout()` returns `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` when the variable is explicitly set and both the request timeout and the process budget are zero. This covers the API server, multi-API-server/headless, and DP supervisor paths, plus the `RemoteOpenAIServer` test budget, because they all call this function.
- If the variable is unset, nothing changes: CUDA still gets 0 s and ROCm still gets 15 s. A positive `--shutdown-timeout` whose remaining budget has run out still gets no extra grace.
- The log line no longer says "ROCm", since the grace can now apply on any platform.

Validated on MI300X, `facebook/opt-125m`, `vllm serve` started under the ci-infra#685 ROCm kernel recorder, one completion, then SIGTERM. To reproduce the CUDA behaviour on ROCm, the harness sets `ROCM_ENGINE_PROCESS_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_S = 0` in the API server process. Each run counts whether the EngineCore recording ends with the recorder's `# end` footer, which is written by the exit hook and never runs after SIGKILL.

| Config (TP=1, 10 runs each) | EngineCore footer | force-killed | SIGTERM to server exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, 0 s grace, `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30` | 0/10 | 10/10 | 0.82 s median |
| this PR, 0 s grace, env unset (default) | 0/10 | 10/10 | 0.77 s |
| this PR, 0 s grace, `VLLM_WORKER_SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=30` | 10/10 | 0/10 | 2.84 s (2.52-3.27) |
| this PR, ROCm default (15 s), env unset | 10/10 | 0/10 | 2.82 s |

With TP=2 (3 runs each), the env var takes runs from 15/24 footered recordings to 24/24. Without it, EngineCore and both TP workers, which own the kernel names, are killed. Shutdown takes 0.87 s without the grace and 6.93 s with it. The grace is an upper bound: shutdown takes as long as EngineCore actually needs to tear down.

commits.pr_title: [CI][ROCm] Fail the AITER nightly overlay on wheels ci_base cannot load
commits.pr_body:
- `aiter-nightly-overlay.sh`: after installing the nightly wheel, run `ldd` on every AITER shared object and fail the overlay build (exit 11) if any required glibc or libstdc++ symbol version is missing from ci_base

Since ROCm 10 became the default image in #58761, the AITER nightly overlay picks `+rocm10.0.0` wheels. Those are built on Ubuntu 24.04 (`GCC 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1`, UFB manifest `glibc: 2.39`) and need `GLIBC_2.38` and `GLIBCXX_3.4.31`, while ci_base is Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35, `GLIBCXX_3.4.30`). They install cleanly, then every test that loads an AITER module fails. In AITER nightly 15218, 135 of 137 failed jobs died with `version 'GLIBCXX_3.4.31' not found (required by .../aiter/jit/module_aiter_core.so)`, including LM Eval KV-Offload Medium and MoE Kernels Shard 3, and the 10-19, 10-20 and 10-21 nightlies look the same. With this check the AITER nightly fails at the overlay step, naming the exact missing versions, instead of failing about 137 tests in ways that look like vLLM bugs. Making it green needs ROCm 10 AITER nightlies built for glibc ≤ 2.35, as the `+rocm7.2.3` ones already are (GCC 11.4 on Ubuntu 22.04). That is a fix for the AITER nightly builds, not for vLLM. A newer libstdc++ alone is not enough, because 13 modules (MHA varlen forward, FMHA v3, hipbsolgemm, f4gemm) need glibc 2.38. #61939 moves this install into `Dockerfile.rocm`, and the same check belongs there once it lands.

Validation: I ran the generated `RUN` line under `/bin/sh` (dash) against three AITER builds. The `0.1.27+rocm10.0.0` nightly from 10-22 fails with 96 missing versions (82 `GLIBCXX_3.4.31`, 13 `GLIBC_2.38`, 1 `CXXABI_1.3.14`). The `0.1.27+rocm7.2.3` nightly from 10-21 and the AITER built into the current ROCm 10 image pass with none. I didn't run the overlay end to end. A first attempt that loaded each module with `ctypes` also rejected the working in-image AITER, because modules depend on symbols from other AITER modules, so this checks symbol versions only. No open PR covers this; #61939 rewrites the step but keeps the same selector. `bash -n`, shellcheck and pre-commit pass.
