## Overview

Deprecate `ir_op_priority` (`--ir-op-priority`) as the first step toward removing vLLM IR. Nothing changes functionally: the option still works and now logs a one-time warning that it will be removed in v0.34.0.

## Claims

- Setting `ir_op_priority` through `--ir-op-priority`, `EngineArgs(ir_op_priority=...)`, or `EngineArgs(kernel_config=KernelConfig(ir_op_priority=...))` logs a one-time deprecation warning.
- Users who don't set it see no warning. Platform defaults and internal `replace()` copies of `KernelConfig` (e.g. the spec-decode draft config) don't trigger it.
- The `--ir-op-priority` help and the config reference, both generated from the field docstring, and `docs/design/vllm_ir.md` now say it is deprecated.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k ir_op_priority`: 2 passed. The new test fails without this change.
- `pytest tests/test_config.py tests/config/test_config_utils.py -k "ir_op or kernel"`: 7 passed.
- End to end on GB200: `vllm bench throughput --model Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --input-len 128 --output-len 32 --num-prompts 16 --enforce-eager`
  - Without the flag: no warning (5.78 req/s).
  - With `--ir-op-priority.rms_norm vllm_c`: one warning from `arg_utils.py`, and the priority is still applied (5.87 req/s).
- `vllm serve --help=ir-op-priority` shows the deprecation note.
- `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

- The warning is raised in `EngineArgs.create_engine_config()` after the top-level `ir_op_priority` has been merged into `kernel_config` and before platform defaults are applied. At that point every non-empty entry was set by the user. A pydantic validator on `KernelConfig` would also fire on `dataclasses.replace(kernel_config, ...)` once the platform defaults are filled in, which would warn users who never set the option. The test covers that case.
- Users who construct `VllmConfig`/`KernelConfig` directly, without going through `EngineArgs`, won't see the warning.
- Duplicate check: no open PR or issue proposes deprecating `ir_op_priority` or vLLM IR (searched for "vLLM IR" and "ir_op_priority deprecate").
- Follow-ups: move the IR ops back to `CustomOp` dispatch, retarget the fusion-pass patterns, then delete `vllm/ir` and the option.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Model] Muse Spark: share one RoPE cache sized by max_model_len
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The ROCm Muse Spark model builds a separate fp32 RoPE cache in each of its 46 sliding-window attention layers. Each cache is sized for 1,048,576 positions, whatever `max_model_len` is, for about 11.5 GiB per GPU. This PR shares one cache across those layers and sizes it by `max_model_len`. Follow-up to #62622.

## Claims

- About 11.5 GiB per GPU is freed for the KV cache pool: from 46 caches of `[1048576, 64]` fp32 to one `[max_model_len, 64]` cache. That is 8 MiB at `max_model_len` 32768 and 192 MiB at 786432. This is an estimate from tensor sizes and has not been measured on a GPU. With `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_ROPE=1`, the per-layer bf16 copies, about 5.75 GiB more, are shared too.
- Numerics are unchanged. Every row of the cos/sin table is computed the same way regardless of its length, and positions never reach `max_model_len`.
- The DSpark draft is unchanged: it keeps its own cache at its current size.

## Validation

The new test builds two target attention layers. It requires them to hold the same `RotaryEmbedding` instance and that instance's cache to be fp32. It fails on the base commit and passes with this PR:

```
$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py -q      # base 2de0531d81
E   assert RotaryEmbedding(head_size=64, rotary_dim=64, max_position_embeddings=4096, base=500000.0, is_neox_style=False ...) is RotaryEmbedding(...)
FAILED tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py::test_target_layers_share_fp32_rope_cache
1 failed

$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_shared_rope.py -q      # this PR
1 passed

$ pytest tests/models/test_muse_spark_rocm_loading.py tests/transformers_utils/test_muse_spark_config.py -q
21 passed
```

These runs were CPU-only, in the ROCm image with no GPU attached. Because of that, the ROCm architecture query and device detection were stubbed locally. The new test is wired into the "Basic Models (Other)" Buildkite step and its MI355 mirror. The MI355 mirror now also lists `vllm/models/muse_spark/` as a dependency.

**Not yet done:** a GPU run comparing the KV cache size reported at startup before and after, and an accuracy check such as GSM8K with greedy output compared against the base. Both are needed before this PR leaves draft.

## Details

**Root cause.**
- Each target `MuseSpark1xAttention` constructs its own `RotaryEmbedding` (`vllm/models/muse_spark/amd/model.py:491`).
- The decoder layer passes it `max(config.max_position_embeddings, max_model_len)` (`amd/model.py:707`), and the checkpoint sets `max_position_embeddings` to 1,048,576.

**Changes.**
- **Size.** Target layers use `max_model_len`. The target RoPE is unscaled, and the scheduler keeps input positions below `max_model_len`, including padded speculative-decoding verify slots (`vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py:770`).
- **Sharing.** Target layers get their RoPE from `get_rope`, which returns one instance per configuration (`vllm/model_executor/layers/rotary_embedding/__init__.py:84`). All sliding-window layers use theta 500000, so there is one cache.
- **Draft.** DSpark draft layers keep their own instance and the larger size, because draft blocks can run past `max_model_len`. Keeping them separate also means the draft's unfused RoPE path cannot recast the target's shared table.
- **Guard.** The fused QK-norm/RoPE/KV-insert path asserts that the shared table is still fp32. The kernel accepts either fp32 or the qkv dtype, so a recast table would otherwise silently switch it to bf16 RoPE.

**Related PRs.**
- #63078 stops the unfused attention path and the DSpark context-key precompute from replacing the fp32 table with a bf16 copy. It complements this PR: that PR keeps tables fp32, and this one makes the target share a single, smaller table. The two edit different hunks of `amd/model.py`. Both add `vllm/models/muse_spark/` to the MI355 step's dependencies, so whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.
- No other open PR shares or resizes the Muse target RoPE cache, so this is not a duplicate. #62064 resized the cache for the NVIDIA path of the superseded #61879, and main has no NVIDIA Muse path.

**Test limitation.** The test replaces the TP linears and the attention backend with `nn.Identity`, and passes a `SimpleNamespace` config. That keeps the test CPU-only and free of a checkpoint, but conflicts with `tests/AGENTS.md`'s preference for real constructors, and is noted for reviewers.

## KV cache and GSM8K: main vs this PR

**Setup.** 8x MI355X, TP8, `amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4`, no speculative decoding. Image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-df6603f05` (aiter 0.1.26, torch 2.13.0+rocm10.0.0), with each tree's Python overlaid; base is main 2de0531d81. Server flags are the AMD MXFP4 recipe's:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 VLLM_ROCM_MUSE_MOE_REDUCE_DTYPE=bf16 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 \
vllm serve amd/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-Quark-MXFP4 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dtype bfloat16 --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --language-model-only --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE"}' \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --enable-chunked-prefill --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --max-model-len 32768 --max-num-seqs 128 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90

# 5-shot, all 1,319 questions, max 256 tokens, 64 concurrent requests
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --temperature 0
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 64 --temperature 1.0 --seed 42
```

Accuracy is shown ± one binomial standard error (n = 1,319). Sampled runs also use the model's default `top_k` 64 from its generation config.

**KV cache at startup**, from the server log:

| Code | Available KV cache memory | GPU KV cache size | Max concurrency at 32,768 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| main 2de0531d81 | 167.67 GiB | 8,173,209 tokens | 249.43x |
| this PR | **179.17 GiB** | **8,733,353 tokens** | **266.52x** |
| difference | **+11.50 GiB** | **+560,144 tokens (+6.9%)** | **+17.09x** |

The measured +11.50 GiB per GPU matches the 46 x [1048576, 64] fp32 tables this PR removes (11.5 GiB).

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Mamba] Avoid re-marking committed prompt-tail boundaries as cached this step
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On hybrid models with `mamba_cache_mode="align"` (e.g. Qwen3.5), requests whose prompts share their last hash-aligned boundary are admitted one per engine step once that boundary is committed. This hits reads fanned out over one prompt and the children of a parallel-sampling request (`n > 1`). This PR skips re-caching that boundary in `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` when the block already carries its hash, so these requests are admitted together. Related: #29387 (the same-step guard this interacts with), #61192 (`/v1/systemone` reads over one state, which take this path).

## Claims

- Bug fix: requests that hit an already committed prompt-tail boundary are no longer deferred, so a fan-out over a shared prefix is admitted together instead of one request per step. Which blocks are cached and hit does not change.
- `vllm bench serve` on Qwen3.5-4B: 5.0x request throughput for a fan-out over shared prefixes with 1-token outputs, 3.0x with 64-token outputs, and 4.7x for parallel sampling with `n=16`. Median TTFT drops 5–15x.
- No accuracy change: on `/v1/systemone` decisions, flips against a serial reference stay at noise level (1/458 vs. 2/458, same max |Δp|), and accuracy is 0.891 with and without the fix.

## Validation

**Reproducer.** Qwen3.5-4B on one RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, `main` at 81c2bd702 with and without this PR, one fresh server per variant:

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B --enable-prefix-caching --max-model-len 8192 \
    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.30 --max-num-seqs 256

# Fan-out: 24 prefixes x 16 prompts, each prefix's prompts sent together.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dataset-name prefix_repetition --prefix-repetition-prefix-len 592 \
    --prefix-repetition-suffix-len 48 --prefix-repetition-num-prefixes 24 \
    --prefix-repetition-output-len 1 --num-prompts 384 --disable-shuffle \
    --max-concurrency 128 --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1

# Parallel sampling: 64 prompts of 640 tokens, n=16.
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 640 --random-output-len 32 \
    --num-prompts 64 --max-concurrency 8 --extra-body '{"n": 16}' \
    --request-rate inf --ignore-eos --seed 1
```

The default `max_num_seqs` exceeds the Mamba cache blocks available at this memory share, hence `--max-num-seqs 256`. The 592-token prefix is one 576-token hybrid block plus 16 tokens, so each prompt's last hash boundary (576) lies inside the shared prefix and away from the prefix/suffix junction, where re-tokenization could shift it. Engine steps are the `/metrics` delta of the `iteration_tokens_total` count. Mean ± std over seeds 1–3:

| workload | output len | variant | req/s | median TTFT (ms) | P99 TTFT (ms) | engine steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| fan-out, 384 prompts | 1 | main | 36.31 ± 0.72 | 3341 ± 127 | 3646 ± 21 | 342 ± 6 |
| | 1 | main + fix | **181.31 ± 7.42** | 649 ± 28 | 832 ± 22 | 42 ± 4 |
| | 64 | main | 23.71 ± 0.66 | 3729 ± 157 | 4852 ± 449 | 763 ± 15 |
| | 64 | main + fix | **70.78 ± 0.06** | 353 ± 12 | 783 ± 3 | 222 ± 1 |
| parallel sampling, n=16, 64 prompts | 32 | main | 1.52 ± 0.02 | 3871 ± 26 | 4232 ± 81 | 1952 ± 0 |
| | 32 | main + fix | **7.10 ± 0.04** | 264 ± 1 | 551 ± 8 | 293 ± 1 |

Prefix-cache hit rates are the same with and without the fix (0.844, 0.900 and 0.844 for the three rows).

**Tests** (on 81c2bd702):

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_mamba_align_siblings_hit_committed_boundary_in_one_step` fails on `main` (`sibling 0 was deferred`) and passes with the fix. A producer commits a 2-block prefix in step 1; in step 2 it finishes its prompt and three siblings hit the committed boundary.
- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/`: 475 passed, including the GPU end-to-end `test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py` (`[base]` and `[mtp]`).
- `pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py`: all hooks pass.

The new test is marked `cpu_test`, so it runs in the existing `v1/core` CPU step in CI.

**Model evaluation.** `/v1/systemone` on `main` (0d00d8b9c): 458 questions over 30 long states (four RACE-middle passages per state, 1,200–1,600 tokens, about 15 questions per request), 8 requests in flight. The serial reference uses `--max-num-seqs 1` without prefix caching.

| | main | main + fix |
|---|---|---|
| questions/s | 36.35 | 57.10 (+57%) |
| p50 request latency | 3.22 s | 2.06 s |
| accuracy | 0.891 | 0.891 |
| decision flips vs. serial reference, max \|Δp\| | 1/458, 0.087 | 2/458, 0.087 |

<details>
<summary>Earlier end-to-end runs: main 0d00d8b9c, v0.32.0 sweep, 27B decision model</summary>

Our own harness: N prompts share a prefix that ends on a hybrid block boundary, plus a 64-token suffix each, sent as token IDs to `/v1/completions` with `max_tokens=1`, 8 groups of 16 in flight.

**main (0d00d8b9c), Qwen3.5-4B, 576-token prefix, N=16:**

| | main | main + fix |
|---|---|---|
| reads/s (prefix-cache hit rate) | 41.96 (0.84) | 235.03 (0.84), 5.6x |
| engine steps for 384 requests | 361 | 25 |
| mean running requests | 1.07 | 15.98 |
| mean queue time per request | 1.98 s | 0.18 s |

**v0.32.0, Qwen3.5-4B (528-token hybrid block), reads/s.** A dense Qwen3-4B on the same harness reaches 239.9, 195.3 and 126.8 reads/s at N=16 for the three prefix lengths.

| prefix (tokens) | fan-out | v0.32.0 | v0.32.0 + fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 528 | 16 | 37.4 | 239.3 |
| 1056 | 16 | 37.6 | 184.3 |
| 2112 | 16 | 35.0 | 128.7 |
| 528 | 4 | 35.6 | 112.8 |

**v0.32.0, 27B Qwen3.5-hybrid decision model (`openjev/openjev`, 784-token hybrid block):**

| | v0.32.0 | v0.32.0 + fix |
|---|---|---|
| fan-out reads/s | 17.4 | 36.6 |
| engine steps for 384 requests | 384 | 24 |
| `/v1/systemone` long-state questions/s | 9.44 | 13.06 |
| decision flips vs. serial reference (458 questions) | 0 | 0 |

Throughput without prefix reuse (distinct cache salts) is unchanged: 47.0 reads/s on `main` (4B) and 5.5 reads/s on v0.32.0 (27B).

</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** `MambaManager._cache_partial_tail_block` re-caches the prompt's last hash-aligned boundary whenever a request whose prompt passes that boundary is scheduled. The request's block at that boundary may already carry exactly that hash, either because it is a prefix-cache hit or because the request committed it in an earlier step. Nothing new is written in that step, but the function still returns the hash. `cache_blocks` then adds it to `cached_blocks_this_step`, and `get_num_blocks_to_allocate` defers every other request whose hit ends on that block (the guard from #29387). This repeats whenever the producer's next chunk or a sibling is scheduled, so siblings are admitted one per step. Because the deferral is reported as insufficient blocks, the scheduler also stops scanning the waiting queue for that step. We found it by logging each deferral with the step that had added the hash: every one pointed at a re-cache of a block already keyed at that boundary.

**Fix.** In the non-checkpoint branch, return early when `source_block.block_hash_num_tokens == num_tokens`. The checkpoint branch above already uses the same condition.

**Why this is safe.** The skip applies only when the block already carries the hash for exactly this boundary, so its state was written in an earlier step or arrived as a hit. A sibling scheduled in this step reads it after that write, since forwards run in order. A step that does write the state still marks the hash, either through the first `cache_partial_block` call for a mid-block boundary or through the full-block loop in `cache_blocks`, so the #29387 guard still applies where it is needed.

**Not a duplicate.** The open PRs that touch `_cache_partial_tail_block` or `cached_blocks_this_step` fix other problems:

- #52972 and #53158 add a similar check to the full-attention manager's `_cache_partial_tail_block`, for stale partial hashes after full-block promotion.
- #56525 replaces the same-step set with a commit fence. The re-mark would still re-publish the hash there and fence siblings until the step commits, so the two changes compose.
- #61282 keeps the boundary state alive until the request ends.
- #55142, #52244 and #53802 change when or where the boundary is registered (connector loads, MTP, EAGLE).

None of them skips the re-cache in `MambaManager`'s non-checkpoint path. RFC #55697 and #55873/#55875/#55876 add application-declared checkpoints with producer/consumer scheduling; this fix is for the default path, with no markers.

**Scope.** The gain depends on siblings arriving together. With many unrelated prefixes interleaved, the bug still admits about one sibling per prefix in each step before the first deferral, so the gap shrinks. In a shuffled `prefix_repetition` run (24 prefixes of 1200 tokens with 64-token suffixes, otherwise as above), main and the fix were within noise: 105.6 ± 6.5 vs. 108.4 ± 5.2 req/s with 1-token outputs, and 35.4 ± 0.2 vs. 36.4 ± 0.9 req/s with 128-token outputs. That run is also close to compute-bound, since each sibling recomputes 112 tokens.

A sibling that arrives in the same step as the producer's first write is still deferred by the #29387 guard, as intended. We also tried letting the scheduler skip a deferred request instead of stopping the scan; with this fix in place it gave no further gain, so it is not included.

**AI assistance.** AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to investigate the issue, write the change and the test, and run the benchmarks. The submitter reviewed every changed line, ran the regression test, and reviewed the results reported here.

The analysis covered 1,524 amd-ci builds since Sep 25 and 14,541 job logs from Oct 10-20. 

For each group and checkpoint-size bucket, the median model-loading time defines the normal load baseline. A run is affected when a same-size load takes more than 2x baseline and adds more than 120 seconds. Normal runtime is the median of successful jobs without an affected load, while affected runtime is the median job runtime among affected runs. Groups were ranked by the total runtime above normal accumulated by affected runs, divided by all observed runs, with at least 15 runs required to avoid low-sample outliers.

AI-assisted tooling was used to analyze the historical CI job metadata and logs; the results and proposed changes were manually reviewed.

Automatically apply the existing `beam` label to Reflection AI Beam pull requests and issues. Extends the labeling approach in #51459 with Beam-specific paths and title patterns.

## Claims

- Label PRs touching Beam's implementation, configuration, Python/Rust parsers, tests, or recipe.
- Label model-specific PR and issue titles, while avoiding ordinary beam-search titles and paths.
- Keep issue matching title-only so pasted logs and configuration in bodies do not trigger the label.

The existing `beam` label (description: "Reflection Beam model support") had no automatic rule. File rules cover the current Beam tree without broadly matching every path containing `beam`.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Tool Parser] Preserve large integer tool arguments
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Preserve large integer tool arguments when their JSON Schema type is `number`.

`coerce_to_schema_type` currently sends every `number` value through `float`
before converting integral results back to `int`. Integer-form values above the
IEEE-754 exact range are silently changed. For example:

```text
input:  9223372036854775807
before: 9223372036854775808
after:  9223372036854775807
```

JSON Schema permits integers wherever `number` is accepted, and Python's JSON
encoder can preserve these values exactly. The change therefore tries `int`
first and falls back to the existing floating-point path for decimal and
exponent forms. Existing behavior remains unchanged for values such as `5.0`,
`1e3`, `3.14`, and non-finite inputs.

The shared conversion function is used by the parser engine and directly by the
K2 Horizon tool parser. Regression coverage exercises the K2 Horizon JSON and
XML formats in both streaming and non-streaming modes.

Related to #47179, which discusses Python/Rust tool argument coercion parity.
The Rust number converter already parses valid JSON integer literals without an
intermediate `f64` conversion.

### Duplicate-work check

I checked #47179 and searched open PRs for references to that issue, large
integer tool parsing, number precision, and `coerce_to_schema_type`. No open PR
addresses this precision-loss case. #47203 changes Rust union-type precedence,
and #53729 resolves property schemas inside combinators; neither changes this
integer conversion path.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py -q
.venv/bin/python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/tool_parsers tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py -q
pre-commit run ruff-check --files vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py
pre-commit run ruff-format --files vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py
pre-commit run typos --files vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py
```

## Test Result

Before the implementation change, all four new K2 Horizon cases failed and
returned `9223372036854775808` instead of `9223372036854775807`:

```text
4 failed, 26 passed
```

After the change:

```text
tests/tool_parsers/test_utils.py:              183 passed
tests/tool_parsers/test_k2_horizon_tool_parser.py: 30 passed
ruff check:                                    passed
ruff format:                                   passed
typos:                                         passed
```

Model evaluation is not applicable. This changes deterministic post-generation
tool argument coercion and does not alter inference, sampling, or model output.

AI assistance was used for this change. I reviewed the diff and test results.

commits.pr_title: [Spec Decode] Keep drafters within their rotary cache on the V2 model runner
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Keep V2 drafters from reading past their rotary cache when the target is served with a longer context (#57941). Where it's safe, the drafter's `max_position_embeddings` is raised to the target's `max_model_len`. Otherwise, on Model Runner V2, the engine's `max_model_len` is lowered to the drafter's, with a warning.

This incorporates the generalization from #57964 by @twu3202 (co-author on the second commit).

## Claims

- The `max_position_embeddings` override that already exists for EAGLE (#48894) now applies to every method except `draft_model`, including DFlash, DSpark and MTP. It's applied only when all of the drafter's RoPE types use that value just to size the cache: `default`, `linear`, `llama3`, `ntk`, `proportional`.
- On V2, any other drafter with a `max_model_len` below the target's lowers the engine's `max_model_len`, with a warning. That covers independent `draft_model` drafters and drafters whose RoPE type can't be extended (yarn, dynamic, longrope, ...). Today such a drafter crashes the engine with an illegal memory access on the first request past its limit.
- V1 is unchanged. It skips speculation past the drafter's limit (`_input_fits_in_drafter`), so the target's `max_model_len` stays as it is.

## Validation

- `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_limits_max_model_len.py` (new, CPU):
  - `draft_model` (2048) with an 8192 target: `max_model_len` is 2048 on V2 (this fails without the change) and stays 8192 on V1.
  - EAGLE-3 drafter (2048) with an 8192 Llama-3.1 target on V2: the cache is raised and `max_model_len` stays 8192. With the RoPE type treated as not extendable, `max_model_len` is lowered to 2048.
- `tests/config/test_speculative_draft_max_position_embeddings.py` (from #57964): which RoPE types allow raising the cache, and DFlash/DSpark drafters inheriting a 65536 target context.
- TODO: CI test results, and an end-to-end repro (`Qwen/Qwen3-4B` at 65536 with `z-lab/Qwen3-4B-DFlash-b16`, and with a `draft_model` drafter, sending a request longer than the drafter's limit).

## Details

Root cause: `SpeculativeConfig` sets `draft_model_config.max_model_len = min(draft, target)`. On V1, the model runner turns that into a check that skips speculation for longer batches. The V2 speculators never read the drafter's `max_model_len`: they clamp positions and sequence lengths against the target's, so they keep drafting past the drafter's rotary cache.

- **Raise when possible:** drafters other than `draft_model` take the target's positions. For cache-only RoPE types, `max_position_embeddings` only sizes `cos_sin_cache`, so raising it doesn't change the rotary frequencies. Other RoPE types either size the cache from `original_max_position_embeddings` or derive frequencies from `max_position_embeddings`, so raising it there would be wrong.
- **Otherwise cap:** making V2 skip speculation per batch would be less restrictive, but it adds branching to every V2 speculator. Capping `max_model_len` at config time is simple and safe. The tradeoff is that such deployments can't serve sequences longer than the drafter's limit even without speculation, and the warning says so. The check lives in `VllmConfig` because only it knows which model runner is in use. `SpeculativeConfig.draft_shares_target_positions()` holds the same condition as the override, so the two stay in sync.
- An explicit speculative `max_model_len` below the target's also caps the target, unless the drafter's cache is raised; V2 ignores that setting in that case.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][CPU] Match GPU conv-state layout in GDN spec decode
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

On CPU, the GDN speculative-decode path updates the conv state with a different layout from the GPU `causal_conv1d_update`. The two agree only when a row has the full `num_spec + 1` tokens. Any shorter row, such as one where the drafter proposed fewer tokens, or a decode row with no drafts that MRV2 still keeps as a spec row, makes the next step read the wrong conv history. If the previous step accepted more tokens than the row now has, it crashes:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (6) must match the size of tensor b (5) at non-singleton dimension 1
```

#62888 started running the MRV2 kernel warmup on CPU. That warmup always produces such a row, so `CPU-Spec Decode` (`tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py::test_v2_speculator_smoke[mtp]`) has failed at engine startup on every main build since [96655](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96655). See the [log in 96693](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96693#01a164c7-7cb9-4409-9585-8ef607bba33f).

This PR makes the CPU path write the conv state with the GPU layout.

## Claims

- CPU GDN spec decode convolves over exactly the accepted token history for any per-row token count `1..num_spec+1` and any `num_accepted`. Previously it crashed when `num_accepted > query_len`, and returned wrong conv outputs after a row shorter than `num_spec + 1`.
- `test_v2_speculator_smoke[mtp]` gets past the startup warmup again.
- Full-length batches still use the native AMX / Arm BF16 kernel.

## Validation

aarch64 (Grace, Arm BF16), CPU build of this branch.

| Check | `main` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| new `test_spec_forward_conv_tracks_accepted_tokens[False/True]` (fallback / native) | both fail with the CI error above | pass |
| same test with only short rows, no `num_accepted > query_len` (local variant) | both fail: about 66% of conv outputs mismatch the reference | pass |
| `tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py` | – | 152 passed |
| `test_v2_speculator_smoke[mtp]` | fails in CI since 96655 | passes in this PR's CI on x86 ([96896](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/96896#01a16926-8cf0-46a1-ae34-e412ab8a5ba9), 4 passed). Not run locally: aarch64 triton-cpu cold-compiles the warmup kernels for over 4 h |

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py
VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE=16 VLLM_CPU_CI_ENV=1 \
  pytest -v -s "tests/v1/e2e/test_cpu_spec_decode.py::test_v2_speculator_smoke[mtp]"
pre-commit run --files vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/cpu/gdn_attention.py tests/kernels/mamba/cpu/test_cpu_gdn_ops.py
```

The new test runs several spec steps with uneven per-row token counts and accepted counts. For each step it compares `_spec_forward`'s conv output against a naive `F.conv1d` over the true accepted history. The CPU SSM kernel is stubbed out, since it does not touch the conv state.

## Details

**Layout.** The conv buffer is `(dim, state_len)` with `state_len = width - 1 + num_spec`. Each step reads its history at column `num_accepted - 1`. The GPU kernel then writes `[history[1:], x]`, i.e. `width - 2 + q` columns, from column 0, so the next step's offset lands right after the accepted tokens. The CPU fallback instead wrote `[B[num_accepted : ...], x]` right-aligned to the end of the buffer. That only matches when `q = num_spec + 1`, and when `num_accepted > q` it produced a slice one column short, which is the crash. The fallback now writes `conv_in[:, 1:]` (the history it just read plus `x`) from column 0. The native `causal_conv1d_update_cpu` kernel also right-aligns, and it rejects `num_accepted > seqlen`. It is now used only when every row is full-length, where the two layouts are identical. Mixed-length batches already used the fallback, so in practice this adds the fallback only for batches where every row is equally short.

**Why CI broke now.** MRV2 keeps decode rows without drafts as spec rows (`q = 1`) carrying the previous step's `num_accepted` (`mamba_hybrid.py`). `warmup_kernels` runs an all-spec step and then a mixed step in which one request has no drafts, so warmup always reaches the crash. Serving reaches the same state whenever a request gets fewer drafts than `num_spec`.

**Relation to #56518.** That open PR handles `num_accepted == 0` in the same fallback loop, so the two will conflict textually. The cases are independent, and whichever lands second needs a trivial rebase.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs and issues for `_spec_forward`, `gdn_attention cpu`, `CPU GDN conv`, `test_cpu_spec_decode`, `62888` and `cpu spec decode mtp`. Only #56518 touches this code, for a different case.

No model evaluation: the e2e smoke test above exercises MTP on Qwen3.5-0.8B, and the unit test checks the conv outputs against a reference.
